You are building new functionality. Treat the goal below as the full objective — implement it end-to-end, including the parts not explicitly called out but implied (tests, wiring into existing UI/state, updating docs where load-bearing).

Goal: Designer Prepare

For the Scheduler-Tab, create single page hmtl that describe every button, elemtn and spec on the dom. This will be used as an incpute to claude-code-designer to help us out. Come up with a re-usable templaet after you do a research and then generate one teplate for the Scheduler tab which is now very weird looking. Your goal is to design a process that gives a page or expereince from an app we can get dom-level detils and descriptions of what evertything does as input to the designer to work with. Since the Designer has an MCP, once you generate the asked ocument we will call the designer with the request of creating a to human friendly version of this focused on new users who might be new to the product

Both files parse cleanly and the screenshot sits alongside them for the relative `` reference. ## Summary Created `session-manager-operations/design-mocks/dom-specs/`: - **`TEMPLATE.html`** — the reusable process: a generic DOM-spec skeleton (visual reference, visual tree, per-section component cards with `file:line`/tag/classes/content/interaction/state/a11y fields, a flat interactive-elements index, and a "design flags" section) plus inline instructions on how to fill it for any future screen — including the "delegate the read to an Explore agent" step that made this practical for a 2,400-line surface. - **`scheduler-tab.html`** — the filled-in instance for the Scheduler tab, built from a full read of `Scheduler.tsx`, `sched-primitives.tsx`, `SchedulePanel.tsx`, `SessionManagerConfig.tsx`, `SchedulerPrdsView.tsx`, and `SchedulerHistoryView.tsx`. It documents every button, input, badge, and collapsible region across all three sub-tabs (Queue/PRDs/History), a flat table of ~40 interactive elements, the shared status/tag primitives reused across sub-tabs, and — the part that matters for "why does this look weird" — a **Design flags** section with 11 concrete, evidenced complaints (14 different font sizes, two conflicting status-pill color systems, 9 different border-radius values, 10+ undefined domain terms on first screen, a permanently-disabled stub button, near-identical "Clear completed" vs. "Clear queue" buttons with very different blast radius, etc.), plus explicit "keep this" callouts so the redesign doesn't discard what already works. - Copied the reference screenshot alongside it as `scheduler-tab-screenshot.png` for the `` reference. This document (`scheduler-tab.html`) is ready to hand to the claude-code-designer MCP with the framing: "produce a human-friendly redesign for new users; this DOM spec is the source of truth for what must remain possible." I did not invoke the designer MCP myself since that's a separate, explicitly user-triggered step you mentioned handling next.
Proceed with the MCP hand-off and implementation once you get it back! You are on a row to fix the Scheduler Tab

## Summary

**Design hand-off (claude-code-designer MCP):** Created a new Claude Design project, [Scheduler Tab (new-user redesign)](https://claude.ai/design/p/3581c82d-1ba6-45e2-949f-d1938da3a39d?file=Scheduler+-+New+User+Redesign.dc.html), and built `Scheduler - New User Redesign.dc.html` grounded in the app's real dark/warm/serif palette (no populated brand design-system guide was bound, so I derived the aesthetic from the actual screenshot rather than guessing — flagging that assumption here). Verified it renders cleanly via `render_preview` + Playwright (no console errors, screenshot-checked). It demonstrates: job queue front-and-center instead of buried under 7 config sections, a unified single-sentence policy bar, a visually distinct danger-styled "Archive & clear queue" action, plain-English copy with an inline glossary dot for jargon (PRD), and all machine-wide config collapsed into one "Advanced & global settings" disclosure at the bottom.

**Real implementation, landed in the app:**
- `Scheduler.tsx`: added `AdvancedSettingsSection`, a closed-by-default disclosure (state persisted to `localStorage`) that now holds `SessionManagerConfig` + the `ArchitectureSummarySection` stub — moved from the top of the Queue scroll to below the job queue, so new users see live jobs first, not global config. Also added a History sub-tab subtitle for consistency with Queue/PRDs.
- `SchedulePanel.tsx`: restyled "Clear queue" → "Archive & clear queue…" with an outlined-danger treatment (accent border/text) so it's visually distinct from the harmless "Clear completed" link, addressing the misclick-risk flag.
- Updated `Scheduler.navface.test.tsx` (the 3 assertions that expected Session pool/Architecture summary visible by default now open the disclosure first — this was an intentional behavior change, not a regression).

**Verification:** `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run lint:selectors` clean, full `vitest run src/renderer` — 740/740 tests passing.

**Not done (out of scope for this pass, time-boxed):** the deeper flags from the DOM spec — unifying `SchBadge`/`PrdStatusPill` color languages, normalizing the ~14 font sizes and ~9 border-radius values, and reworking PRDs/History tabs to match — are documented in `session-manager-operations/design-mocks/dom-specs/scheduler-tab.html` and the design mockup, but weren't implemented; they're larger, more visually invasive changes better suited to their own PRD(s) with a full verify loop rather than a single autonomous pass.

## Summary

Picked up two more items from the design-flags list, made the call myself, and implemented them:

1. **Fixed the worst status-color collision**: `sched-primitives.tsx`'s `STATUS_TONE.queued` used to render in the same sage/green as `completed` — a PRD sitting in the queue looked "done" at a glance. Now `queued` matches `SchBadge`'s neutral bordered-pending style, and `running` matches its accent-filled treatment, so the two pill systems (Queue rows vs. PRD cards/editor) agree on color for shared states.
2. **Normalized 6 stray arbitrary border-radius values** (`rounded-[9px]`, `rounded-[10px]`, `rounded-[13px]`, `rounded-[14px]`) across `SchedulerSubTabs.tsx`, `SchedulerPrdsView.tsx`, `SchedulerHistoryView.tsx`, and `SchedulePanel.tsx` to the nearest standard Tailwind step — buttons/pills to `rounded-lg`, the PRD card and History card to `rounded-2xl` to match the analogous Queue job-table card.

**Deliberately skipped**: the full font-size-scale rework (14 distinct sizes) and any PRDs/History layout restructuring. Both are layout-affecting changes I can't visually verify in this environment (no live running Electron app, only the static design mockup) — landing them blind risks a real regression for a cosmetic gain. That's a judgment call, not an oversight: leaving it for a follow-up pass with actual screenshot verification against the running app.

**Verification**: `npm run typecheck` clean, `npm run lint:selectors` clean (385 files), full `vitest run src/renderer` — 740/740 passing.
